subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Which public provider-family fallback contract should OpenClaw support for model failover, if any: wildcard/auto refs, grouped fallbackFamilies, catalog-derived fallbacks, or explicit flat fallbacks only?
rationale: Current code has a flat fallback contract, while the issue and discussion propose multiple incompatible public config shapes that affect provider/auth routing and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Choose one core fallback contract
options.body: Select a single canonical design and require schema, runtime, docs, and migration/doctor alignment before implementation.

options.title: Limit scope to explicit flat fallbacks
options.body: Decline wildcard or grouped fallback config for now and improve docs or diagnostics around manual fallback maintenance instead.

options.title: Treat catalog-derived fallback as separate
options.body: Review the existing catalog-derived fallback pull request as a narrower partial feature without closing this broader provider-family request.

recommendation.title: Choose one core fallback contract
recommendation.body: Select a single canonical design and require schema, runtime, docs, and migration/doctor alignment before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal on model fallback, config schema, docs, and agent runtime ownership points to steipete for the product boundary decision.
